$comment: One state, one movement, one answer. The cases that break naive implementations, and every refusal the module can produce, each reachable by handing the function the bad state directly rather than by hoping the data can reach it (CONVENTIONS §6). `state` is built as a moving-average file unless `layers` is given, in which case it is used verbatim — that is how a state the strategy could never have produced gets in front of the code that guards against it.

cases.name: issuing one thousandth more than is on hand
cases.why: negative stock is refused, not priced. One thousandth over is the input that this condition and nothing else excludes

cases.name: issuing exactly what is on hand
cases.why: the boundary is inclusive, and the whole value leaves. A greater-than-or-equal refusal would fail here

cases.name: issuing one thousandth less than is on hand
cases.why: 1000.00 x 9.999 / 10.000 is exactly 999.90, and a thousandth of a unit still carries ten paise

cases.name: issuing from an item holding nothing
cases.why: there is nothing to take out and no average to take it at

cases.name: issuing nothing from an item holding nothing
cases.why: 0 out of 0 is the division this module must never perform. It is legal and it costs nothing

cases.name: a receipt onto an empty item sets a fresh average
cases.why: nothing on hand means nothing to average against

cases.name: a receipt of nothing at no cost changes nothing
cases.why: the average is untouched, and 1000.00 over 7.000 is the recurring case the unit-cost scale exists for

cases.name: freight capitalised onto stock on hand
cases.why: a real inward movement with no quantity: the average rises without a unit arriving

cases.name: a cost with no quantity to carry it
cases.why: the same movement onto an EMPTY item would leave value against nothing on hand — invariant 6, refused while somebody can still fix it

cases.name: a free sample lowers the average
cases.why: a zero cost is a real receipt. 100.00 a unit becomes 66.666667

cases.name: stock worth nothing is still stock
cases.why: quantity without value is ordinary and must be VALUED, not refused. This is the half of invariant 6 that is legal

cases.name: value with nothing to hold it
cases.why: the mirror of the case above, and the one that is NOT legal: no movement here can produce it, so the register and the ledger have diverged

cases.name: a negative quantity on hand
cases.why: the value is fine and the quantity is not; this condition alone excludes it

cases.name: a negative value on hand
cases.why: the quantity is fine and the value is not; the other half of the same pair

cases.name: layers that do not add up in quantity
cases.why: the aggregate and the breakdown are both stored precisely so this can be false and be said out loud

cases.name: layers that do not add up in value
cases.why: the quantity check alone would pass this, which is why there are two

cases.name: a layer holding a negative quantity behind a positive total
cases.why: the aggregate is positive and adds up, so only a per-layer check can see it. This is the row the FIFO strategy will produce if it consumes a layer twice

cases.name: a layer valued below nothing behind a positive total
cases.why: and the value half of it

cases.name: a movement carrying a negative quantity
cases.why: invariant 3: which way the stock went is on the kind, and a minus sign is a second answer to a question already answered

cases.name: a movement carrying a negative cost
cases.why: a credit is a movement the other way, not a receipt with a minus in it

cases.name: an inward movement with no cost
cases.why: invariant 4. Without this refusal `statedCostOf` would value the goods at nothing

cases.name: an outward movement carrying a cost
cases.why: the other half of invariant 4: a caller that could price its own sale could make the register and the ledger disagree at will

cases.name: a quantity carrying a fourth decimal place
cases.why: rejected rather than rounded, so the card recomputed from the stored rows equals the card computed when they were written

cases.name: a cost carrying a third decimal place
cases.why: and the money scale, which the quantity check alone would let through

cases.name: a state whose quantity carries a fourth decimal place
cases.why: the same rule on the way in from a table, not only on a movement

cases.name: a state whose value carries a third decimal place
cases.why: and its money half

cases.name: a movement naming a layer this item does not hold
cases.why: moving average holds one pool. A movement aimed at a layer it does not have is refused rather than pooled anyway

cases.name: a movement naming the pool itself
cases.why: a movement replayed from a stock ledger row carries the layer it hit, and the pool is a layer it can legitimately name

cases.name: a movement carrying a batch number
cases.why: a batch number recorded against a pool is a number nothing can ever act on. Refused rather than accepted and dropped

cases.name: a movement dated on a day that does not exist
cases.why: April has thirty days. The card is folded in date order, so a movement with no real date has no place in it

cases.name: a purchase return leaves at the average
cases.why: the pool has no memory of what was paid for these particular units. The supplier is credited at the price on the debit note; the difference is a variance for the posting rule

cases.name: a sales return comes back at the cost it left at, not today's average
cases.why: the average on hand is 200.00 and the goods sold at 100.00. Taking them back at 200.00 would credit cost of goods sold with 500.00 more than was ever charged to it

cases.name: an adjustment out is valued like any other outward movement
cases.why: shrinkage leaves at the average, and the average does not move

cases.name: an adjustment in states its cost
cases.why: a stock-take surplus brought in above the average lifts it, exactly as a receipt would

cases.name: opening stock states its cost
cases.why: an opening balance is a movement like any other, so a card can be replayed from nothing
